update.ready: A new version of mccontrol is available.
update.failed: Could not keep a copy for offline use: {reason}
key.passphrase.hint: At least {min} characters. You need it to unlock the key and to open the backup.
key.fingerprint.enable: Also unlock with fingerprint or face
key.fingerprint.disable: Stop unlocking with fingerprint or face
key.persist.granted: The browser keeps the key's storage.

stats.title: Statistics
stats.intro: Traffic, battery and uptime from Beacon, which reads the Observer feed. Nothing is sent to the mesh.
stats.nodeHint: The first 8 characters of the node's public key, for example 4AC61A7F.
stats.unknown: Beacon does not know this node.
stats.noStatus: This node has never published a status to Beacon.
stats.chartTitle.24h: Airtime sent per hour, last 24 hours
stats.chartTitle.7d: Airtime sent per 6 hours, last 7 days
stats.chartLabel: Bar chart of airtime sent. The arrow keys read the bars one at a time.
stats.summary: {tx} s of airtime sent and {rx} s received over {period}.
stats.source: Source: Beacon. Every number is as old as the node's last status.
dash.att.notHeard: not heard on MQTT for {hours} h
dash.att.noAnswer: no answer to the last command ({command})
dash.att.forged: bad signature on the answer to {command}: forged or altered
node.noKey: There is no key in this browser yet.
node.noWholeKey: Only the first 8 characters of this node's key are known, so commands go unencrypted (v1). Find it again with discovery to learn the whole key.
node.noFacts: Nothing read yet. Send ver, get name or get autoreply.
node.noHistory: Nothing sent to this node from this browser.
node.nameHint: Your name for it here. The name the mesh sees is changed with set name.
node.regionHint: Only lou-19 and older need it: the IATA code their observers use, e.g. JKG. Not needed once the node runs lou-20.
node.forgetBody: It leaves the list and its groups. The node keeps your key and still obeys it; its history stays.
nodes.caption: Your {n} nodes
nodes.empty: No nodes yet. Find them below, or add one by its key.
nodes.refreshFleet: Battery and last heard from Beacon
nodes.discoverExplain: Reads the alive messages your lou-20 and later nodes keep on the shared command server and opens the ones sealed to your key, wherever the node is. A node sends one soon after it connects and then about every 15 minutes. Nothing is sent and nothing goes on the air.
nodes.discoverNone: None of your nodes has an alive message on the command server. Nodes on lou-19 and older, and mesh-only nodes, leave none: add them by their key.
nodes.keyChanged: answered under another key: the stored key is kept
nodes.addByKey: Add a node by its public key
nodes.name: Name
nodes.uplink.mesh: No: commands go over the mesh
nodes.uplinkHint: A node on lou-20 or later with Wi-Fi and remote control on is found by itself and need not be added here. Without Wi-Fi a command goes through one of your nodes that has MQTT, or through a companion radio. You can change this later in the node's settings.
send.title: Send
send.lede: A command to one node, several, a group, or each of your nodes in a county. It is checked before it is signed.
send.advanced: Each of your nodes in a county (advanced)
send.regionExplain: One sealed command per node, in random order, 10 to 90 s apart (5 to 30 min for a restart), to each of your nodes that names this county as its region home. Commands that transmit, and the mesh road, are refused.
send.toRegion: Each of your nodes in the county
send.commandHint: Start typing for the list of commands, e.g. ver, get autoreply, region.
send.lacks: This node's image ({version}) has no {feature} feature: it will answer not-allowed.
send.notAdmitted: This node runs {version}, which does not admit this command; it needs {needs}. It will answer not-allowed.
send.maybeUpdated: If the node has been updated since, send ver first.
send.oldLogin: This node is spoken to the old way: it runs lou-20 but has left no alive message, so its command connection most likely still uses the old login. It will answer, but not everything works. The cure is set cmd on and reboot on its console or from an admin login in the MeshCore app; lou-21 repairs it by itself.
send.res.clockHint: Its radio was heard within the hour, so the node is up but off the command server. Its clock may have fallen behind after a restart: send time through a relay or a companion, or check its Wi-Fi.
send.someRefuse: {n} will answer not-allowed by their firmware: {names}.
send.v2: Goes encrypted (v2): the node's firmware opens it and its whole key is known.
send.v1: Goes signed but readable (v1): older firmware, or only part of the key is known.
send.perNode: One signed command to each of the {n} nodes in turn, on its own topic.
send.broadcastNote: One sealed command to each of your {n} nodes in {region}, one node at a time.
send.confirmRegionTitle: Send to each of your nodes in {region}?
send.confirmRegionBody: Each of your {n} nodes in {region} gets its own sealed command, in random order and spaced out, so this takes a while.
send.silenceNote: No answer means none arrived in time, not that the node did not run it.
send.locked: The key is locked. Unlock it to sign.
send.res.silentHelp: Nothing came back in time. The node may be off the command server, or answered late.
send.res.forgedHelp: The line on this node's result topic was not signed by its key: forged or altered. The reply was ignored.
send.res.noHelp: The node refused it; see Help for this code.
send.res.finding: This firmware should admit it: the table or the version is wrong.
send.res.tooOldHelp: This node runs {version}, which does not admit {command}; that came in {needs}. Flash a newer firmware to use it.
send.res.maybeOld: Its firmware is not known here; {needs} or newer admits it, so an older image refuses it.
send.why.broadcastTransmit: a command that transmits goes to one node at a time, never to each node of a county
send.why.noRegion: {name} runs lou-19 or older and no IATA code is known for it yet: read its status from Beacon, or update it to lou-20
send.why.oldAscii: {name} runs {version}, which takes plain ASCII only; letters such as åäö need lou-17
send.why.broker: the command server could not be reached: {detail}
send.why.badRegion: a region is its IATA code, 2 to 8 letters or digits
send.why.otaRefused: this node cannot be updated over the control plane: {detail}
history.caption: Commands sent and what came back, newest first
history.keepExplain: The history lives only in this browser. Export it to keep a copy or move it; an import adds what is not already here.
history.importHint: Events already here are skipped; events of another key are left out.
history.imported: Imported {added}; {skipped} already here or unreadable; {foreign} of another key.
groups.none: No groups yet. A group lets you send to several nodes in one go, each on its own topic.
groups.name: Name
groups.sendExplain: One signed command to each of the {n} members in turn. A member that cannot take it is reported and the rest still get it.
groups.deleteBody: Only the group goes; its nodes stay.
sets.title: Command sets
sets.pickTarget: Choose a node or a group
sets.argHint: Put in every step where {arg} stands.
sets.name: Name
sets.nameHint: One word. A set with the same name is replaced.
sets.stepsHint: At most {n}. {arg} is asked for when the set runs.
update.title: Firmware
update.unknown: The version is not known yet. Send ver to read it.
update.byHand: {latest} is out. This node cannot take an update over remote control: its firmware admits ota update there from lou-19. An Observer node with Wi-Fi can update itself when ota update is typed on its own console (USB); any node can be flashed by hand.
update.confirmBody: From {from} to {to}. The node downloads the image, restarts, and is off the air and off the control plane for a few minutes. If the new image fails, it goes back to the old one.
update.byHandShort: not over remote control: how to update
update.stage.otaCheck: Asking the node whether an update fits it…
update.stage.restarting: The node took the update and is restarting.
update.stage.checking: Asking its version, {secs} s after the start
update.stage.timeout: The node has not reported the new version yet; it still says {version}. Check again later with ver.
update.stage.cancelled: Stopped waiting; the node may still be updating.
node.statsLink: Battery, airtime and noise floor from Beacon
help.codesBody: Every answer from a node carries one of these codes. The explanations are in English, as in the terminal tool.
help.english: This text is the same in every mccontrol interface, the terminal tool included, and is in English.
help.intro: These texts are the same in every mccontrol interface, the terminal tool included, and are in English.
help.name: Name
help.noTopic: There is no help text called {name}.
keyscreen.askKeep: Ask the browser to keep it
keyscreen.backupConfirmed: You said the key is saved elsewhere ({at}).
keyscreen.changePassNote: A backup file saved before the change still opens with the old passphrase only.
keyscreen.copyFailed: Could not copy. Select the text and copy it by hand.
keyscreen.cost1: Every node set up with this key stops obeying you. Move them to a new key first, with "Replace the key on your nodes" on this tab. Older nodes need the new key over USB.
keyscreen.cost2: This browser forgets the current key the moment the new one is stored.
keyscreen.cost3: Without a copy of the current key (the backup file, or the key in a password manager), it is gone once replaced.
keyscreen.fingerprintBody: Unlock with your fingerprint or face instead of typing the passphrase. The passphrase still works and is still needed for everything else.
keyscreen.fingerprintHow: The browser asks for your fingerprint or face twice: once to make a passkey, once to check that it opens the key. Nothing is stored unless both work.
keyscreen.fingerprintNo: This browser cannot unlock with a fingerprint here: {reason}
keyscreen.fingerprintOn: The key also unlocks with your fingerprint or face on this device.
keyscreen.helpLink: How signing works, and what the key protects
keyscreen.isUnlocked: The key is unlocked in this tab.
keyscreen.keepRefused: The browser did not promise to keep it. Keep the backup safe.
keyscreen.none: There is no key in this browser yet.
keyscreen.publicBody: This is what a node is given so it obeys you. It is not secret.
keyscreen.qrHint: Scan it with a phone to move the public key to another device.
keyscreen.qrLabel: QR code of the public key
keyscreen.replaceBlock: Replace the key in this browser
keyscreen.replaceBody: Make or import another key in place of this one. Read what it costs before you do.
keyscreen.replaceTitle: Replace the key in this browser?
keyscreen.toSetup: Put this key on a node
settings.autoLockHint: A job that is running when the time is up finishes first.
settings.badHost: Write a host name such as mqtt.example.se, with :port if it is not 443.
settings.badRegion: A region is 2 to 8 letters or digits, such as JKG.
settings.brokersBody: Commands go to the shared command server, wherever your nodes are. An own command server set up for lou-19 and older nodes is listed here until those nodes run lou-20.
settings.brokersHelp: When you use your own command server
settings.displayBody: These belong to this device. Setup's Display tab has the same choices.
settings.hostHint: A host name, with :port if not 443. Secure WebSocket (wss) only, path /.
settings.lowBattery: Warn when the battery is below
settings.lowBatteryHint: The overview lists a node whose battery is under this voltage. Default {v} V.
settings.notHeard: Warn when a node has not been heard for
settings.notHeardHint: Heard means on MQTT: a node can be on the air with its MQTT link down. Default {h} hours.
settings.regionHint: 2 to 8 letters or digits, such as JKG.
settings.removeLabel: Remove your own command server for {region}
setup.firefox: Firefox asks once to install a site permission before it lists serial ports.
setup.handBody: On an iPhone, an iPad or any browser without USB access here: open a serial console to the node at {baud} baud and type these two lines, each followed by Enter. For lou-20. Older: set mqtt.cmd.pubkey, set mqtt.cmd on.
setup.handReply: The node answers "OK" to the first line. If the second answers "reboot to apply", type reboot.
setup.intro: A node obeys only the public key it was given over its USB console or, the first time, from a logged-in admin. The node refuses an admin's key while its admin password is the default, shorter than 8 characters or the same as the guest password. Nothing secret leaves this browser.
setup.keyNotSeen: The console does not show this key yet. Read what the node answered above.
setup.keyTitle: The key to put on the node
setup.noKey: Make or import a key first; this is where it goes onto a node.
setup.noSerial: This browser cannot reach USB serial ports. Chrome, Edge and Firefox 151 or later on a computer can; an iPhone or iPad cannot. Use the lines below.
setup.ownRegion: A node that uses your own command server takes a different second line.
setup.rebootWhen: Reboot appears once the node answers "reboot to apply". Each button sends one line; nothing is sent otherwise.
setup.step1: Connect the node to this computer with a USB cable.
setup.step2: Close any other program that has its serial port open, such as a flasher or a terminal.
setup.step3: Press Connect and choose the node in the browser's list.
setup.thenBody: Once the node has rebooted and joined the command server, it answers to this key. The board finds it by itself on the next look, or at once with Look now in STATUS. A node without Wi-Fi answers mesh only to get cmd and is never found: add it yourself, with its public key, and reach it through a relay or your companion radio.
unlock.backupNeedsPass: The file is encrypted with this passphrase; it asks for it when opened.
unlock.backupPassHint: It opens the file and then protects the key in this browser too.
unlock.fingerprintFailed: The fingerprint or face sign-in did not open the key. Use the passphrase.
unlock.forgotBody: Nobody can recover it: the key is encrypted with it, here and in the backup. If you know the passphrase of a backup file, import that file. Otherwise make a new key; every node set up with this one then needs the new key over USB.
unlock.importBody: A backup file from this page or the terminal tool, or the 64 hex characters of the terminal tool's key.seed.
unlock.intro: mccontrol signs commands with a key that lives in this browser, encrypted with your passphrase. Make a new key, or bring in the one you already use: a backup file or the terminal tool's key.seed.
unlock.kind.backup: A backup file: type its passphrase.
unlock.kind.seed: A bare seed: choose a passphrase to protect it here.
unlock.kind.unknown: This is neither a backup file nor the 64 hex characters of a seed.
unlock.locked: The key in this browser is locked.
unlock.makeBody: Choose the passphrase that encrypts the key here and in its backup.
unlock.noRecovery: Nobody can recover a forgotten passphrase. Keep it where you keep your other passwords.
unlock.pasteHint: The file's text or the seed's 64 hex characters. It stays in this browser.
unlock.problem.short: The passphrase needs at least {min} characters.
unlock.replaceWarn: Every node set up with the current key stops obeying it once the new key is stored.
unlock.savedAs: Saved as {file} in your downloads folder.
unlock.unavailable: This browser does not let the page store a key (private window, or site data turned off).
unlock.wrong: Wrong passphrase, or the file has been changed.
unlock.ownCopy: The key lives only in this browser. Keeping a copy of it, as the backup file or in a password manager, is up to you.
keyscreen.seedBody: For a note in a password manager. Type the passphrase to show it.
keyscreen.seedWarn: Anyone with this key can command every node set up with it.
keyscreen.seedWhen: Hidden again after 60 seconds, when the key locks, when you switch away from this tab or leave this page. A copied key is then cleared from the clipboard.
road.hint: Auto takes the mesh for a mesh-only node, for a repair only the mesh admits, for a node not heard over MQTT for {mins} min, or when the command server cannot be reached. Otherwise MQTT. With no companion connected, Auto can go through a relay that reaches the node without a flood.
road.willMesh: Goes over the mesh through your companion ({why}).
road.willMeshPlain: Goes over the mesh through your companion.
road.meshLimits: Over the mesh: one node at a time, at most 57 bytes (59 to lou-19). A node answers a flooded command 15 to 30 seconds after it arrives, and at most 50 commands an hour.
road.groupMesh: Over the mesh each node is asked in turn.
road.why.meshCommand: only the mesh road admits this command
road.why.notHeard: not heard over MQTT for {mins} min
road.why.mqttUnreachable: the command server could not be reached
road.why.meshClosed: the node's mesh road is closed because its MQTT works, so it was sent again over MQTT
road.contactAdded: The node was added as a contact on your companion; its answer teaches the companion a path.
road.silentMesh: Silence over the mesh is not a refusal.
road.adviceSilent: The node may be out of answer airtime: wait a few minutes, and get cmd counts it under refused. Or the packet was lost on the way.
road.adviceRefused: Since the read before the silence, get cmd counts more under refused: the node refused for lack of answer airtime. Wait a few minutes and send again.
road.adviceFlood.relay: Two direct sends in a row got no answer. The stored path may be stale. Try once with {route} set to {flood}: a flood renews the path.
road.adviceFlood.mesh: Two direct sends in a row got no answer. The stored path may be stale. Try once with {road} set to {relay} and {route} set to {flood}: a flood renews the way.
road.help: Repair a node over the mesh
road.relayHint: A relay is one of your own Observer nodes on MQTT, with the same command key as the node and in radio reach of it. It sends the command by radio and returns the answer. It takes one command at a time and has an airtime budget: about 26 commands in 15 minutes, then 5 in the next 15. A second one sent while the first waits for its answer is refused as busy, or gets no answer; the first goes through.
road.route.path: Direct along the stored path ({hops} hops)
road.routeShort.flood: flooded in the relay's home region
road.routeShort.flood-wide: flooded in the relay's default scope
road.hears.no: not in its neighbour list (it lists only what it heard since it started)
road.hears.guess: not checked; about {km} km away, a guess
road.hearsYes: {relay} hears {target} directly. The route is set to direct neighbour.
road.hearsNo: {relay} does not list {target} as a neighbour. Its list holds only nodes it heard an advert from since it started, so a direct send may still work.
road.hearsUnknown: The answer from {relay} does not settle it: its list is full, or could not be read.
road.budget: {relay} has {left} s of airtime left for now and has sent {floods} of 100 floods today.
road.budgetUnknown: {relay} did not say what is left of its budget.
road.relayNone.relayOff: No relay: relaying is switched off on {name}.
road.relayNone.relayNotHeard: No relay: none of your nodes that can relay has been heard in the last half hour. Find your nodes again.
road.relayNone.relayCannot: No relay: a relay is one of your own Observer nodes on MQTT with lou-20 or later.
road.unchecked: not checked that it hears the node
road.relayPick: Choose a relay and a route.
road.willRelayAuto: Goes through the relay {relay}, {route} ({why}). No companion is connected.
road.relayLimits: Through a relay: one node at a time, only what the mesh road admits, and the relay waits two minutes for the answer.
road.floodBody: {relay} sends this as a flood in its home region. Every node there that hears it sends it on, and that costs all of them airtime.
road.floodBodyWide: {relay} sends this as a flood in its default scope, which is wider than its home region. Every node that hears it sends it on, and that costs all of them airtime.
road.floodBudget: A relay allows one flood a minute for 15 minutes, then one in five minutes, and 100 a day.
road.relaySnr: The relay heard the answer at {snr} dB.
road.relaySilent: The relay did not answer. It may be offline, or run firmware older than lou-20. It is not known whether anything was sent.
road.relayUnread: The relay returned an answer that could not be read with this node's key.
companion.title: Companion radio
companion.connecting: Connecting. Choose the radio in the browser's list.
companion.otherFirmware: The companion restarted but doesn't answer over USB. It probably runs the Bluetooth (or Wi-Fi) companion firmware, which only talks over that link: connect by Bluetooth, or flash the USB companion firmware.
companion.ios: iPhone and iPad browsers cannot reach a companion: none of them has Web Bluetooth or Web Serial. Use a computer, or an Android phone with Chrome or Edge.
companion.unsupported: This browser cannot reach a companion. Chrome and Edge can, by Bluetooth or USB; Firefox from version 151 by USB, after it asks for permission for this site.
companion.usbOnly: This browser has no Web Bluetooth: USB only.
companion.noBluetooth: This browser has no Web Bluetooth. Chrome and Edge have it.
companion.noUsb: This browser has no Web Serial. Chrome and Edge have it; Firefox from version 151.
companion.insecure: The page is not on https here, so the browser offers neither Bluetooth nor USB.
companion.lede: The mesh road sends a signed command to one node over LoRa, through your own companion radio. The connection stays open on this page until you disconnect or leave.
send.why.meshBroadcast: the mesh road goes to one node at a time; a county goes over MQTT
send.why.meshOnlyNode: {name} is mesh only (no Wi-Fi, no MQTT): send it over the mesh
send.why.meshTooLong: over the mesh a command is at most {max} bytes; this one is {bytes}
send.why.meshNoKey: the mesh road needs the whole public key of {name}; discover the node to learn it
send.why.meshOldFirmware: {name} runs {version}; the mesh road needs lou-19 with the control plane (rc)
send.why.noCompanion: no companion is connected: connect it first, or choose the road "relay" to send through one of your nodes with MQTT
send.why.badRoad: choose a road: Auto, MQTT, Mesh or a relay
send.why.relayOne: a relay takes a command to one node at a time, sent by hand
send.why.relayNotHeard: {name} has not been heard in the last half hour: find your nodes again
send.why.relayCannot: {name} cannot relay: a relay is an Observer node on MQTT with lou-20 or later
send.why.relayOff: relaying is switched off on {name}: send it set relay own
send.why.relayFloodConfirm: a flood through a relay must be confirmed first
send.why.relayNoPath: no path is stored for the relay {name}: check its neighbours, or flood once
send.why.relayOldTarget: {name} runs a firmware older than lou-20: a relay reaches lou-20 or later only
settings.meshAfter: Auto road: take the mesh when a node has not been heard over MQTT for
settings.meshAfterHint: Heard means its status on Beacon or its last answer over MQTT. A node opens its own mesh road after 15 minutes without MQTT. Default {m} minutes.
node.regionSetHint: The region's scope name, e.g. se-jkp. Sent as region put, region allowf, region save, then region to read it back.
node.meshOnlyHint: A mesh-only node takes commands over the mesh alone, sealed to it from lou-20 (lou-19 and older: signed for the region named mesh). Its version tells (an rc image without -observer); set it here when the version is not known.

board.tileFailed: This tile could not be drawn: {reason}
tile.noSelection: No node selected. Pick one from the list.
tile.taggedCount: {n} tagged: the command line sends to them
tile.findNodes: Find the nodes that have your key
tile.noBeacon: Beacon has no status for this node.
tile.skipped: {n} cannot take it and are left out: {names}.
tile.noResults: Nothing sent from this browser yet.
tile.noResultsNode: Nothing sent to {name} from this browser yet.
tile.noSuchResult: This result is not in this browser's history.
tile.relaySnr: Answer heard by the relay at
tile.mapEmpty: Your nodes appear here once you have some.
tile.mapNoPositions: Beacon has no position for your nodes yet.
tile.mapBeaconFailed: Beacon could not be reached, so there is no map.
tile.mapCaption: {placed} of your {n} nodes placed, {links} neighbour links, {others} other repeaters
start.failed: mccontrol could not start in this browser
start.reason: The reason, to copy into a bug report:
start.tryAgain: Try reloading the page, or open it in a private window.
setup.tab.node: Put the key on a node
setup.copySelected: The browser refused the clipboard. The text is selected: press Ctrl+C (⌘C on a Mac).
setup.reg.title: Registered with the command server
setup.reg.body: A command server passes on commands only from keys it knows. The page registers the key by itself when it is made or unlocked: one signed message to the command server, nothing on the air.
setup.reg.allOk: Every command server knows this key.
setup.reg.notAll: Not every command server confirmed. The lines above say why.
setup.reg.notYet: Not registered with {host} from this browser yet. It happens when the key is unlocked.
setup.reg.refused: {host} did not accept the key: {detail}. Press Register again; if it says the same, ask whoever runs that command server.
setup.broker.noSocket: This browser cannot open a connection to a command server.
setup.broker.noSocketNext: Use a current Chrome, Edge, Firefox or Safari.
setup.broker.unreachable: Could not reach the command server {host}.
setup.broker.unreachableNext: Check that this device is online. If you use your own command server, check its address under Setup, Command server and companion.
setup.broker.noAnswer: The command server {host} did not answer.
setup.broker.noAnswerNext: It may be busy or down. Try again in a minute.
setup.broker.refused: The command server refused the sign-in ({why}).
setup.broker.refusedNext: Register the key again under Setup, Key. If it is still refused, the command server does not accept this key yet.
setup.broker.noAck: The command server did not confirm the registration in time.
setup.broker.noAckNext: Press Register again under Setup, Key in a minute.
setup.broker.closed: The connection to the command server closed before the answer came.
setup.broker.closedNext: Try again. If it keeps happening, the connection is unstable.
setup.run.regions: Each of your nodes in a county
setup.run.regionWarn: Each of your {n} nodes in {region} gets this, one sealed command each. You are asked once more before it is signed.
sets.what: A command set is a saved list of up to six commands that run one after the other on a node or a group. It stops at the first refusal or silence, so a half-done change is easy to see.
sets.when: Use one for a change that takes more than one command, or that you make on many nodes.
sets.example: Example: the shipped set {set}, run with {arg}:
sets.argExplain: {arg} in a step is asked for when the set runs.
palette.title: Commands
palette.placeholder: Type a command, a setting or a name
palette.sendToHint: to the tagged nodes, or the selected one
palette.regionHint: {n} of yours; asks before it is signed
palette.cmd.ver: Read the firmware version and build.
palette.cmd.get stats: Read the node's counters: packets, airtime, uptime.
palette.cmd.get cmd.mesh: Read whether the node takes commands over the mesh: off, on or auto, and whether the road is open now.
palette.cmd.get alive.interval: Read how often the node sends its sign of life to you, in minutes.
palette.cmd.set autoreply.national: Auto-reply on the national test channel #test-se: auto, off or a region.
palette.cmd.set alive.interval: How often the node sends its sign of life to you: 5 to 1440 minutes.
palette.cmd.get sensors: Read the battery, the temperature and any sensors on the node.
palette.cmd.region: List the regions the node knows and which carry floods.
palette.cmd.neighbors: List the repeaters the node hears directly, with their signal.
palette.cmd.get radio: Read the radio settings: frequency, bandwidth, spreading factor, coding rate.
palette.cmd.get repeat: Read whether the node repeats packets.
palette.cmd.get flood.max: Read the most hops a flood may travel through this node.
palette.cmd.get flood.max.unscoped: Read the hop limit for floods without a region.
palette.cmd.get txdelay: Read the delay factor before repeating a flood.
palette.cmd.get direct.txdelay: Read the delay factor before repeating a direct packet.
palette.cmd.get rxdelay: Read the receive delay base: how much longer a weak reception waits before it is relayed (0 is off, the default).
palette.cmd.get af: Read the airtime factor: how long the node stays quiet after sending.
palette.cmd.get cad: Read whether channel activity detection is on.
palette.cmd.get mqtt.status: Read whether status is published and how each MQTT slot is connected.
palette.cmd.get cmd: Read the command plane's state on the node: on or mesh only, the counter, the last command, and how many requests over the mesh it answered and refused.
palette.cmd.get relay: Read whether the node relays your commands to nodes near it, and what is left of its airtime budget.
palette.cmd.get mqtt.iata: Read the node's IATA region code.
palette.cmd.get mqtt.interval: Read how often the node publishes its status, in minutes.
palette.cmd.get mqtt.presets: Read the broker presets a slot can take (set mqttN.preset <name>).
palette.cmd.ota check: Ask whether newer firmware is available.
palette.cmd.get: Read any setting by its name.
palette.cmd.set autoreply: Turn the auto-reply to test messages on or off.
palette.cmd.set autoreply.mode: How a test that names no mode is answered: flood, private or direct.
palette.cmd.set autoreply.hops: The most hops away a test may come from.
palette.cmd.set autoreply.direct.flood: Answer a test heard directly with a flood, not with one zero-hop packet.
palette.cmd.set autoreply.private: Answer private tests sent to this node alone, or not.
palette.cmd.set autoreply.region: The region the node answers in: the channel #test-<region> and the replies' scope.
palette.cmd.set autoreply.slots: How many reply slots the window is split into.
palette.cmd.set autoreply.window: The reply window, from and to, in seconds.
palette.cmd.trigger test: Make the node send a test now. The letter sets how replies come: F flood, P private, D direct, S none.
palette.cmd.trigger private: Make the node send a private test to one repeater.
palette.cmd.region put: Make a region, under a parent region if one is given.
palette.cmd.region default: The region the node's own messages use.
palette.cmd.region save: Keep the region changes over a restart.
palette.cmd.set txdelay: The delay factor before repeating a flood.
palette.cmd.set direct.txdelay: The delay factor before repeating a direct packet.
palette.cmd.set rxdelay: Receive delay base, 0 to 20: a flood heard weakly waits longer before this node relays it, so a stronger repeater goes first. 0 turns it off (the default).
palette.cmd.set af: The airtime factor: how long to stay quiet after sending.
palette.cmd.set cad: Turn channel activity detection on or off.
palette.cmd.set flood.max: The most hops a flood may travel through this node.
palette.cmd.set flood.max.unscoped: The hop limit for floods without a region.
palette.cmd.set path.hash.mode: Path hash size on packets this node sends itself (not on what it relays): 0, 1 or 2 for 1, 2 or 3 bytes per hop.
palette.cmd.set loop.detect: How hard the node looks for routing loops: off, minimal, moderate or strict.
palette.cmd.set multi.acks: Send an extra acknowledgement: 1 on, 0 off.
palette.cmd.set mqtt.status: Publish the status over MQTT, on or off.
palette.cmd.set mqtt.packets: Publish received packets over MQTT, on or off.
palette.cmd.set mqtt.raw: Publish raw packets over MQTT, on or off.
palette.cmd.set mqtt.neighbors: Publish the neighbours over MQTT, on or off.
palette.cmd.set relay: Relay your commands to nodes near it over the mesh: own (on) or off.
palette.cmd.set mqtt1.preset: MQTT slot 1: a preset or custom.
palette.cmd.set mqtt2.preset: MQTT slot 2: a preset or custom.
palette.cmd.set mqtt3.preset: MQTT slot 3: a preset or custom.
palette.cmd.set mqtt4.preset: MQTT slot 4: a preset or custom.
palette.cmd.set mqtt5.preset: MQTT slot 5: a preset or custom.
palette.cmd.set mqtt6.preset: MQTT slot 6: a preset or custom.
palette.cmd.reboot: Restart the node: off the air until it is back.
palette.cmd.clkreboot: Reset the clock to a fixed old date and restart.
palette.cmd.ota update: Install newer firmware over the network. The node restarts.
palette.cmd.powersaving: Turn power saving on or off.
palette.cmd.gps: Turn the GPS on or off. Only builds with GPS have it; others answer with an error.
palette.cmd.set: Change any setting the console takes.
area.chooseLabel: Area not chosen: choose your county
disc.undone: Removed again. Discovery will not add them back.
mesh.find.title: Mesh-only nodes
mesh.find.lede: A node without Wi-Fi never reaches the command server, so the search above cannot find it. This looks in your companion's contacts and for repeaters Beacon places inside your county that are not observers. It sends nothing. What it finds are possible mesh-only nodes, not confirmed.
mesh.find.looking: Looking: the companion's contacts and Beacon's positions.
mesh.find.noArea: None of your nodes names its county yet, so Beacon is not searched by position.
mesh.find.noContacts: Connect the companion to include its contacts.
mesh.find.fromCompanionHops: in the companion's contacts, {n} hops away
mesh.find.airtime: Check sends one signed ver over the mesh through your companion. It uses airtime, so it goes only when you press it.
mesh.find.needKey: Checking a node needs your key.
mesh.find.needCompanion: Checking a node needs the companion radio.
mesh.find.waitingFor: Sent. Waiting up to {s} s for an answer.
mesh.find.answered: It answered with your key: added to your list as a mesh-only node.
mesh.find.silent: No answer. The node may not hold your key, may be out of reach, or may run firmware without the mesh road.
std.search: Search the nodes by name or public key
std.noNodes: No nodes yet. mccontrol looks for them by itself while your key is unlocked, and "Find more nodes" looks now. A node without MQTT is added by its key.
std.pickNode: {n} nodes. Choose one in the list to see it and send it commands.
std.mapNoPosition: {name} has no known position. The map shows your other nodes.
std.logoutBody: The key is locked. Nothing can be signed or sent until you unlock it again with your passphrase.
std.neighboursLede: Direct: in the node's own neighbors reply. Beacon: seen by observers only. SNR: the last reply, then the average over the stored replies. Send neighbors to ask the node again.
std.noNeighbours: No neighbours known yet. Send neighbors to the node to ask it.
display.cvd: Colour-blind mode: states in blue, yellow and orange, never red and green
help.aboutBody: mccontrol is open source (github.com/sweden-mesh/mccontrol-web). It is built with:

combo.label: Commands
combo.unknown: Version unknown: every command is listed
value.path.hash.mode.0: 1 byte per hop in the paths of packets this node sends (256 ids, up to 64 hops)
value.path.hash.mode.1: 2 bytes per hop in the paths of packets this node sends (65 536 ids, up to 32 hops)
value.path.hash.mode.2: 3 bytes per hop in the paths of packets this node sends (16.7 million ids, up to 21 hops)
value.loop.detect.minimal: drops a flood that already holds this node 4 times (1-byte ids), 2 times (2-byte) or once (3-byte)
value.loop.detect.moderate: drops a flood that already holds this node twice (1-byte ids) or once (2- and 3-byte)
value.loop.detect.strict: drops a flood that already holds this node once
hint.notKnown: Not heard yet: no status known
hint.noAnswerYet: Not heard yet: the last command ({command}) got no answer
nodes.wholeKey: A node is added by its whole public key: 64 hex characters.
report.copied: The status lines are copied. Paste them when you ask for help.
report.refused: The browser refused the clipboard. Select and copy this:
report.hint: Click to copy all status lines
relay.title: Relay
relay.on: This node relays your commands to nodes near it.
relay.off: Relaying is switched off on this node.
relay.unknown: It is not known yet whether this node relays.
relay.explain: A relay sends your command by radio to a node that has no MQTT and returns the answer. About 26 commands in 15 minutes, then 5 in the next 15, and only for you.
send.why.mcc3NoKey: {name} runs lou-20 or later, which needs its whole public key; find your nodes again or add it by its key
send.why.emptyArea: none of your nodes names {area} as its region home
companion.net.addressHint: Where mccontrol-bridge listens: ws://192.168.1.20:8765 with the bridge's IP address, or wss://name:port when it has a certificate.
companion.net.token: The bridge refused the token. Give the one it was started with.
companion.net.tokenHint: Only when the bridge runs with a certificate and a token. Not kept: asked each time.
companion.net.prompt: The first time, Chrome or Edge asks to let this site reach devices on your local network. Allow it; it asks once. If you blocked it, allow it again in the site settings (the icon left of the address).
companion.net.other: Firefox and Safari need wss:// with a certificate the browser trusts; the bridge's README says how.
companion.net.badUrl: Give the bridge as ws://IP:port or wss://name:port.
companion.net.mixedContent: From this page ws:// reaches only an IP address on your own network. Use the bridge's IP address (not its name), or wss:// with a certificate.
companion.net.unreachable: The bridge did not open. Either the browser's local-network permission was refused (allow it in the site settings), the bridge is not running at that address, or it refused this page (its origin, or the address it was reached by).
companion.net.busy: Another page is already attached to the bridge. Close it there and connect again.
companion.net.companion: The bridge cannot reach the companion radio. Is it on, and on the address the bridge was given?
companion.net.tooBig: The bridge closed the connection: a frame was larger than it takes.
companion.net.text: The bridge closed the connection: it takes binary frames only.
install.title: Install as an app
install.body: mccontrol then opens in its own window and works without a network for everything but sending. It changes to a new release only when you press Switch now.
install.installed: mccontrol is running as an installed app.
install.manual: This browser installs from its own menu: in Safari, Share and then Add to Home Screen (iPhone, iPad) or Add to Dock (Mac); in Chrome or Edge, the install mark in the address bar.
install.dismissed: Not installed. The button comes back the next time the page opens.
install.version: Release {version}, commit {commit}. Every file is checked against the release's integrity.json before the offline copy keeps it.
demo.label: Demo
demo.bannerSending: Simulated nodes. Nothing reaches a real repeater.
demo.tryLead: No node flashed and no key yet?
demo.tryAfter: An invented fleet to look around in and send commands to. Nothing leaves this page.
demo.notHere: Not in the demo: its key is invented and lives in this page only.
demo.keyNote: This key is invented and lives in this page only. Making, importing, backing up, showing or changing a key is not in the demo. Replacing the key on the demo's nodes can be tried below.
demo.sendOff: Sending is off in the demo.
demo.noCompanion: A companion radio is not in the demo.
rekey.title: Replace the key on your nodes
rekey.body: Make a new key and move your nodes to it from here, without a visit. The key in use keeps working until you finish.
rekey.how1: Nodes on lou-20 or later take the new key from afar. Older nodes need it over USB.
rekey.how2: A node is first sent the new key, signed by the key in use. Then it is sent one read signed by the new key. When it answers, it is on the new key.
rekey.how3: The new key waits on a node for 60 minutes, or until the node restarts. After that the node forgets it and nothing has changed.
rekey.startPassHint: The new key is stored under the same passphrase. Nothing is sent yet.
rekey.started: The new key is made. Nothing is sent yet.
rekey.saveFirst: Save the new key before any node is told about it. A node that takes it obeys no other key, and this browser can lose what it stores.
rekey.nodesBody: Send to one node at a time. Start with the nodes that are reached through a relay, and take the relays last.
rekey.noNodes: You have no nodes in the list.
rekey.untilFinish: Until you finish, the other screens sign with the key in use. A node on the new key answers only here.
rekey.state.sent: The new key waits on it, not proved. {min} min left
rekey.state.expired: The 60 minutes passed. It is on the key in use again
rekey.state.failed: Did not take the new key. It keeps the key in use
rekey.why.usb: Needs the new key over USB (firmware older than lou-20)
rekey.why.noVersion: Its firmware version is not known. Read it first (ver)
rekey.why.noKey: Its whole public key is not known
rekey.step.offer: The new key, signed by the key in use
rekey.step.prove: A read signed by the new key
rekey.sendAll: Send to the {n} nodes on Wi-Fi, one at a time
rekey.sendAllTitle: Send the new key to {n} nodes?
rekey.sendBody: Two commands go to each node: the new key, then a read signed by it. If the read is answered, the node obeys only the new key from then on.
rekey.proveBody: One read signed by the new key goes to the node. If it is answered, the node obeys only the new key from then on.
rekey.sendAir: This node is reached over the mesh. Each command costs airtime for every node in reach. Nothing is sent again by itself.
rekey.finishTitle: Make the new key your key?
rekey.finishNone: No node has taken the new key.
rekey.finishLeft: Still on the old key: {names}. After you finish they answer only to the replaced key, and need the new key over USB.
rekey.maybeTook: Sent the new key but not proved: {names}. If one of them took it and the answer was lost, it obeys only the new key. Keep the backup file of the new key.
rekey.finishUsb: Cannot take it from here and need it over USB: {names}.
rekey.finishKept: The replaced key stays in this browser, sealed with your passphrase, until you choose to forget it.
rekey.finished: The new key is now your key. The replaced key is kept on the key tab.
rekey.abortBody: The new key is forgotten here and the key in use stays your key. Nothing changes on a node that has not taken the new key.
rekey.abortTaken: {names} already took the new key. Finish the replacement. Aborting now would leave them on a key this browser has forgotten.
rekey.aborted: The new key is forgotten. The key in use is still your key.
rekey.replacedBody: A key you replaced is kept here, sealed with your passphrase. A node that stayed on it answers only to it. To command such a node, download the key's backup file and import it as the key in this browser.
rekey.forgetBody: Without a copy of it, a node that still has this key can never be commanded again without a visit.
rekey.viaCompanion: Over the mesh, through the companion
rekey.viaNone: No companion is connected, and no node of yours can relay to it now without a flood
